_comment_file: The application shell: title bar, tab strip, status bar, footer, inspector, and the two full-area states (empty vault, locked vault). Loaded before the first paint, because it is on screen whenever the window is.

titleBar._comment_: A 38px bar. Every label here is also a tooltip, so short wins — but a disabled control's tooltip says WHY, because 'why not?' is the only question a dead button raises.
titleBar.lockAlreadyLocked: There is no unlocked vault to lock.
titleBar._comment_lockingShort: Shown in the bar itself, where there is room for one word. The tooltip carries lockInProgress.
titleBar._comment_needsVault: {action} is one of the four labels above. Interpolated rather than concatenated: languages differ on where the subject of this sentence goes.
titleBar._comment_controlFailed: SECURITY-ADJACENT. The window controls are the one place where doing nothing is indistinguishable from being broken. Do not soften this into 'something went wrong'.
titleBar.controlFailed: {action} was refused by the window manager.
titleBar.noWindow: This page is not running inside the Remoter window, so the window controls do nothing here.

tabStrip.noSessions: No open sessions — double-click a connection to start one
tabStrip._comment_inspector: Ctrl-free: F4 is a bare function key and is written as-is in every language.
tabStrip._comment_filesOpen: The control that opens a file pane under the session in front. The four 'filesNo…' / 'filesNot…' sentences are the reasons it is doing nothing, one per reason: a disabled control has to say WHY, and 'unavailable' is not a reason. A file pane is one more channel on a connection that has already authenticated, never a second sign-in, which is why three of the four are about the session rather than about the pane.
tabStrip.filesNoSession: Browsing files needs an open session. Double-click a connection to start one.
tabStrip.filesNotRunning: This session is not connected, so there is no connection to browse over.
tabStrip._comment_filesNoFileChannel: SSH and SFTP are never translated. Names the reason rather than saying the button is unavailable.
tabStrip.filesNoFileChannel: This session carries no files. SFTP runs over SSH; an RDP or VNC session has no file channel.
tabStrip.filesIsFileSession: This tab is already a file session.

statusBar.unresolved: Effective values have not been resolved yet
statusBar._comment_protocolUnset: Sits where SSH, RDP, VNC or SFTP would. Lower case: it is the absence of a protocol, not the name of one.
statusBar.showDetail: Show the failure in the inspector

footer._comment_: Counts. Every one is a plural: Russian needs four forms here and Arabic six, and the zero case is worth its own wording in the languages that have one.
footer.sessions: {count, plural, =0 {no sessions} one {# session} other {# sessions}}
footer.tunnels: {count, plural, =0 {no tunnels} one {# tunnel} other {# tunnels}}
footer.connections: {count, plural, =0 {no connections} one {# connection} other {# connections}}
footer.credentials: {count, plural, =0 {no credentials} one {# credential} other {# credentials}}
footer.openPanels: Open the sessions and tunnels panel
footer._comment_locksIn: {clock} is mm:ss, produced by formatClock() so the digits follow the locale's numbering system.

inspector.title: Effective values
inspector.nothingSelectedBody: Choose a connection in the tree to see its resolved settings.
inspector.notAConnection: Folders have no effective values of their own.
inspector.notAConnectionBody: What a folder sets is shown on the connections beneath it, as the source of an inherited value.
inspector.notAskedBody: Resolution runs against an open vault. This one is locked, so there is nothing to resolve against yet.
inspector._comment_unset: The value of a field nobody has set, anywhere in the inheritance chain.
inspector._comment_setHere: Provenance labels, shown under a resolved field. 'set here' means this connection's own value; the others name where an inherited value came from. Lower case: they are fragments under a value, not sentences.
inspector._comment_fromSource: {source} is a folder or connection name — user data, in any script, isolated before it arrives.
inspector._comment_overridesInherited: {field} is a field name such as 'port' or 'username'. This is the case worth calling out: the tree above says something different from what will actually be used.
inspector.credentialShared: set here · shared with other entries
inspector.noFields: This connection resolves to no fields.

emptyVault.title: This vault is empty
emptyVault._comment_body: {vault} is the vault file's name, which is user data and may be in any script. It is wrapped in a Unicode isolate before it gets here, so the sentence keeps its own direction whatever the name contains.
emptyVault.body: Nothing is stored in {vault} yet. Most people start by bringing across what they already have.
emptyVault._comment_importBody: Product and file names. Not translated.
emptyVault.createBody: A host, a protocol and a credential is enough to start.
emptyVault.openBody: Locks this vault and returns to the vault picker.
emptyVault.openFailed: This vault was not locked, so the picker did not open.

main._comment_nothingSelectedBody: Ctrl+K is a key name. Translate the sentence around it, not the key.
main.nothingSelectedBody: Choose a connection in the tree, or press Ctrl+K to search for one.
main._comment_sidebarLabel: The accessible name of the connection tree's landmark region. Read aloud when a screen reader lists the regions of the window.
main._comment_nodeKind: What a selected tree entry is, shown above its name where a connection shows its protocol. These are the node kinds from the domain model; they are shown to the user, so they are translated, unlike the protocol names beside them.
main.connectHint: Double-click it in the tree, press Enter in the palette, or use Connect in its context menu.
main.folderSelected: Folders hold settings that the connections beneath them inherit.
main._comment_lockedBody: SECURITY-CRITICAL wording in one respect: it must keep saying that nothing was lost. A user who believes a lock destroyed their connections will go looking for a backup they do not need.
main.lockedBody: It locked itself after the idle period, or was locked from another window. Nothing was lost; the connections are still in the file and come back when you unlock it.
main.vaultStateFailed: Remoter cannot tell whether a vault is open.
main.treeFailed: The connection tree could not be read.
main.fullscreenFailedTitle: The window did not go full screen.
main.fullscreenFailedBody: The window manager refused it, or this page is not running inside the Remoter window. Nothing about the session changed.
main.checkingVault: Checking whether a vault is open…
main.readingTree: Reading the connections out of the vault…

kdfUpgrade._comment_: SECURITY-CRITICAL SECTION. This is the offer to strengthen a vault's key derivation. Do not soften 'weaker than the current standard' into 'could be improved', and do not drop the sentence explaining why the password is asked for again — a credential prompt without a stated reason is exactly what a phishing dialog looks like.
kdfUpgrade.offer: This vault's key derivation is weaker than the current standard. Strengthening it takes a moment and needs no new password.
kdfUpgrade.dismissLabel: Dismiss this suggestion until the next unlock
kdfUpgrade.passwordHelp: The same password you just unlocked with. Each key slot is rebuilt around it, so it has to be entered again.
kdfUpgrade._comment_working: Short enough that reserving room for it does not widen the idle button.
kdfUpgrade.workingStage: Deriving the key again, at the stronger cost…
kdfUpgrade.readFailed: This vault's header could not be read, so the key slots cannot be strengthened.
kdfUpgrade.keyfileMissing: This vault's password slot also needs its key file.
kdfUpgrade.keyfileDialog: Choose the key file for this vault
kdfUpgrade.keyfileDialogFailed: The system file browser did not open, so no key file could be chosen. Nothing was sent to the vault.
kdfUpgrade.failed: The key slots were not strengthened.
kdfUpgrade.done: Done. This vault's key slots are at the current cost.
kdfUpgrade.blockedKeyfile: Choose the key file this vault needs.
